title: Summarize Environmental Impacts and Local Environment Controls

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Computer equipment can be damaged by heat, humidity, poor ventilation, dust, and power problems. Batteries, toner, and retired electronics also require responsible disposal.
sections.callout: Dispose safely → control the environment → keep it clean → protect the power.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Match installation, maintenance, cleaning, power, and disposal scenarios to the control that protects people, equipment, and the environment.

sections.title: Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)
paragraphs: MSDS documentation provides hazardous-material handling, health, protective-equipment, storage, spill-response, and disposal information. Current workplaces may call it a Safety Data Sheet (SDS).
sections.callout: Material handling and disposal information → MSDS.

entries.title: Proper Battery Disposal
paragraphs: Laptop, mobile-device, and UPS batteries may create environmental and fire hazards. Use approved recycling or disposal and handle swollen batteries carefully; never puncture, crush, or incinerate them.

entries.title: Proper Toner Disposal
paragraphs: Follow manufacturer guidance, workplace procedures, recycling programs, and regulations for used toner cartridges.

sections.title: Proper Disposal of Other Devices and Assets
paragraphs: Computers, monitors, printers, storage, mobile devices, and network equipment belong in approved electronic-waste processes. Sanitize protected data before recycling or disposal.
sections.callout: Data sanitization protects information; approved disposal protects the environment. Retired equipment may require both.

sections.title: Temperature and Humidity-Level Awareness

entries.title: Temperature
paragraphs: Excessive heat causes throttling, shutdowns, damage, and reduced component life.

entries.title: Humidity
paragraphs: Excess moisture promotes condensation and corrosion; overly dry air increases ESD risk.

sections.callout: Too hot → cooling problem; too wet or dry → humidity problem.

sections.title: Proper Ventilation and Location/Equipment Placement
paragraphs: Keep vents clear and avoid crowding equipment or placing it near heat, water, heavy dust, blocked airflow, and physical hazards. Placement should support cooling, safety, access, and security.
sections.callout: Hot air needs a clear path away from equipment.

sections.title: Dust Cleanup
paragraphs: Dust on fans, heat sinks, vents, filters, and internal components restricts airflow and raises temperature. Clean using tools and procedures suitable for electronics.

sections.title: Compressed Air and Vacuums

entries.title: Compressed Air
paragraphs: Use controlled compressed air to blow away loose dust. Prevent fans from spinning excessively.

entries.title: Vacuums
paragraphs: Use only equipment designed for electronics when suction is appropriate; ordinary household vacuums can introduce static.

sections.callout: Blow → compressed air; suitable suction → electronics-safe vacuum.

sections.title: Power Surges, Brownouts, and Blackouts

table.caption: Recognize power conditions
rows: Voltage drops below normal while power remains

sections.callout: Up → surge; down → brownout; gone → blackout.

sections.title: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
paragraphs: A UPS provides limited battery-backed power during an outage so work can be saved, systems can shut down safely, or brief interruptions can be bridged.
sections.callout: UPS provides time, not permanent electricity.

sections.title: Surge Suppressor
paragraphs: A surge suppressor helps protect connected equipment from voltage spikes.
sections.callout: Temporary battery power → UPS; voltage-spike protection → surge suppressor.

sections.title: Environmental Protection Workflow
bullets: Consult MSDS/SDS and use approved disposal
Provide clear ventilation and suitable placement
Use a UPS for temporary power and a surge suppressor for spikes

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Too wet or dry → humidity control

sections.title: Objective 4.5 Exam Trap
bullets: Surge means voltage up, brownout means voltage down, and blackout means power gone.
UPS supplies temporary battery power; a surge suppressor controls spikes.
Low humidity increases ESD risk; high humidity increases moisture and corrosion risk.
Temperature is heat level; ventilation moves heat away.
Use electronics-safe cleaning tools rather than assuming a household vacuum is suitable.
Data destruction and environmental disposal solve different requirements.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
sections.callout: Dispose safely → control the environment → keep it clean → protect the power.
